```python name=advanced/serialization.py
# ============================================================
# PICKLE — Serialize Python objects to bytes
# ============================================================
import pickle
import shelve
import json

# --- Pickle: Save any Python object ---
data = {
    "users": [{"name": "Veera", "scores": [90, 85, 92]}],
    "metadata": {"version": 1, "timestamp": "2026-04-19"},
}

# Serialize (dump)
with open("data.pkl", "wb") as f:
    pickle.dump(data, f)

# Deserialize (load)
with open("data.pkl", "rb") as f:
    loaded = pickle.load(f)

# To/from bytes
bytes_data = pickle.dumps(data)
restored = pickle.loads(bytes_data)

```

# ⚠️ SECURITY WARNING: Never unpickle untrusted data!
# pickle.loads() can execute arbitrary code.

# --- Custom pickling ---
class Connection:
    def __init__(self, host):
        self.host = host
        self.socket = None  # Can't pickle sockets!
    
    def __getstate__(self):
        state = self.__dict__.copy()
        del state["socket"]  # Remove unpicklable
        return state
    
    def __setstate__(self, state):
        self.__dict__.update(state)
        self.socket = None  # Reconnect later

# SHELVE — Persistent dictionary (uses pickle internally)
with shelve.open("mydata") as db:
    db["users"] = ["Alice", "Bob"]
    db["config"] = {"debug": True}

with shelve.open("mydata") as db:
    print(db["users"])   # ['Alice', 'Bob']

# JSON vs PICKLE comparison
# JSON:
#   ✅ Human-readable, cross-language, safe
#   ❌ Limited types (no datetime, set, custom classes)
#
# Pickle:
#   ✅ Handles ANY Python object
#   ❌ Python-only, binary, SECURITY RISK
